name: Straddling or Overriding Tricuspid Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Straddling or Overriding Tricuspid Valve

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of tricuspid valve leaflets overriding the interventricular septum
Presence of a ventricular septal defect associated with abnormal tricuspid valve insertion
Right ventricular hypertrophy detected by imaging or ECG
Central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunting

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of tricuspid valve overriding or straddling with associated ventricular septal defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on detailed echocardiographic assessment; cardiac MRI may be used for further anatomical delineation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunting
searchTerms: blue skin from heart blood mixing
central cyanosis due to heart shunt

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to tricuspid valve malformation
searchTerms: heart murmur from malformed tricuspid valve
systolic murmur due to tricuspid problems

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance or dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: difficulty exercising or shortness of breath

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.symptomName: Hepatomegaly secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: liver swelling due to right heart problems

occasional.symptomName: Ascites due to right-sided heart failure
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from heart failure
ascites due to right-sided heart issues
stroke caused by abnormal blood clots
stroke due to embolism crossing heart

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels indicating cardiac strain
Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia due to right-to-left shunting
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating overriding or straddling tricuspid valve leaflets
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and right ventricular enlargement
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with congenital heart defect syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy and possible arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Downward displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets rather than overriding
Pulmonary stenosis with overriding aorta instead of tricuspid valve
Ventricular septal defect with aortic override

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of right heart failure in infancy
Recurrent syncope or stroke suggestive of paradoxical embolism
references: Anderson RH, et al. The anatomy of straddling and overriding tricuspid valve. Heart. 2010;96(2):123-129.
